opener_concept: Saving pocket money to afford a game: common sense gives the fewest whole weeks (a whole RANGE, 3 or more, not one number), naming the answer as an inequality solved just like an equation; a second box finds the boundary value, and the reveal previews the sign-flip warning.
notes: All 20 problems fresh-solved and correct in the live row before edits; the two counting answers the audit called degenerate (silver[2]=3->5, gold[0]=4->5) were already 5 live, so no maths repair was needed there. Audit fixes applied: (1) removed the non-firing 'didnt_flip' misconception from every problem without a negative multiply/divide (all 8 bronze, silver counting + S6, all gold except G1); it survives only on S0, S1, S3, S4, G1 where a real flip exists. (2) Renamed the misleading number-line 'wrong_integers' pattern to 'strict_vs_nonstrict' on multiple-choice problems and rewrote the message to be about the strict-vs-nonstrict symbol the student picks (no number line drawn). (3) Rewrote the counting-problem 'wrong_integers'/arithmetic messages (silver[2], gold[0]) to name the real error: excluding/forgetting negative integers. Dropped one arithmetic misconception on G2 whose stored expect (option x<2) did not reproduce from any clean slip. Every remaining misconception expect was re-derived by committing the error and confirmed to equal a wrong option index (MC) or a determinate wrong value. Stripped all em dashes (method_card, misconception messages, worked_examples step labels '—' -> ':'). Added guided infrastructure: opener, three teach walks (bronze two-step solve, silver the negative-division flip, gold listing integers across a double inequality including negatives), tier_guides for all three tiers, hints on all 20 problems, and guided_steps with a completion boundary on the 4 single_value problems (silver[2], silver[5], gold[0], gold[3]); multiple_choice problems carry no guided_steps per spec. Preserved related_videos and topic_links byte-for-byte; worked_examples changed only to remove em dashes. Validator PASS; every guided box independently recomputed and lands on stored solutions.
